## Context

Parent epic `a4bd-4ca8-c44f-49bb`; depends on S1 (`248f-ac00-18db-4259`). S3
(`47a0-7019-da4b-40e0`) makes the inbound removal path decline removals of links carrying no
peer-confirmation record. Without a backfill the FIRST post-upgrade pass would find an empty
store and decline EVERY legitimate peer deletion — a regression worse than the blind spot being
fixed. The epic states the requirement directly: "Backfill grandfathers existing managed links as
confirmed-at-upgrade (marked as such) so the first post-upgrade run does not decline every
legitimate removal."

This story must land BEFORE S3 turns the decline on.

## Scope

- `peer_confirmations.py` — the loader records whether the store file was ABSENT at open time
  (e.g. a `was_absent` attribute set in `open_store`). Backfill runs on "file was absent" (a
  fresh upgrade), NOT on "store is empty": an operator who legitimately emptied the store must
  not silently have it re-populated.
- `peer_confirmations.py` — add
  `backfill_from_managed_refs(store, local_tickets, binding_store, pass_id) -> int`, returning
  the number of records written. For each local ticket, read its managed refs via
  `rebar.reducer._managed_refs.managed_ref_set(ticket)` (whose kinds are already constrained to
  `MANAGED_REF_KINDS`, so no extra kind filter is needed or wanted). For each `(kind, target)`
  whose `target` resolves to a BOUND peer key via `binding_store.get_jira_key(target)`, write a
  record keyed `(ticket_local_id, target, kind)` with `source="backfill"`,
  `direction="backfill"`, `link_id=None`, `confirmed_pass=pass_id`, `confirmed_at=<now ns>`.
  Records are explicitly MARKED as backfill so a later audit can distinguish grandfathered
  evidence from proven evidence — this is a requirement, not a nicety.
- `reconcile.py::_persist_and_log` — invoke it inside the existing `if persist:` block, at the
  same seam S2 uses (beside `_advance_baselines`, before `binding_store.save()`) and BEFORE the
  S2 snapshot-confirmation call, so a genuine snapshot observation in the same pass can upgrade
  a backfilled record's provenance. Wrapped in the same fail-open `try/except Exception` shape
  (log to stderr, never break a sync pass).
- A backfilled record is treated as confirmed by `is_confirmed()`. Distinguishing backfill from
  proof at the DECISION point is deliberately NOT done — that would re-open the blind spot for
  every pre-upgrade link, which is precisely what grandfathering exists to avoid.
- `managed_refs` monotonicity is unchanged; nothing is pruned.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 On a store whose file was absent, every managed ref with a bound target gets a record
      with `source="backfill"` and `direction="backfill"`; the store is then non-empty and
      persisted. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_backfill.py -k fresh_upgrade`.
- [ ] AC2 A managed ref whose target is UNBOUND gets no record. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_backfill.py -k unbound`.
- [ ] AC3 Backfill does NOT run when the store file existed but is empty. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_backfill.py -k existing_empty`.
- [ ] AC4 Backfill does not re-run on a subsequent pass once the file exists — a second pass adds
      zero backfill records. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_backfill.py -k second_pass`.
- [ ] AC5 A later snapshot confirmation for a backfilled key overwrites `source` to `"snapshot"`;
      a backfill never overwrites an existing `"push"` or `"snapshot"` record (provenance
      upgrades, never downgrades). Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_backfill.py -k provenance`.
- [ ] AC6 `is_confirmed()` returns True for a backfilled record. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_backfill.py -k confirmed`.
- [ ] AC7 In no-write mode (`persist` False) no backfill is written. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_backfill.py -k nowrite`.
- [ ] AC8 Every edited module stays under the 800-line cap. Proof: `bash -c 'git archive HEAD |
      tar -xO src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile.py | wc -l'` per edited file, < 800.
- [ ] AC9 Gates green. Proof: `make lint` exit 0, `make typecheck` exit 0,
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler` exit 0.

## Testing

- New suite `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_backfill.py` covering the
  fresh-upgrade backfill, the unbound-target skip, the existing-but-empty non-run, one-shot
  behavior across two passes, provenance upgrade/no-downgrade, `is_confirmed` acceptance, and
  the no-write path.
- Regression: `make lint && make typecheck && pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler`.

## Out of scope

The removal decline (S3). No pruning of `managed_refs`. No change to its monotonicity.
